query: Starting from a multi-element automotive alloy catalyst containing multiple principal elements in nearly equiatomic ratios, what single intervention could overcome activity loss and durability limitations while maintaining low platinum-group-metal consumption during transient and low-temperature gasoline or hybrid-vehicle exhaust operation, including exposure to H2O and NO and degradation associated with thermal aging or increasing mileage? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the untreated starting catalyst, boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Inverse-model guided selection of multicomponent catalysts synthesized under high alkalinity and moderate temperatures will induce beneficial Cu–Pt electronic cooperation, minimizing deactivating Pt–Ni/Fe interactions and enhancing redox buffering. This results in improved low‐temperature hydrocarbon oxidation and NO reduction after severe ageing compared to a Pd/Al2O3 benchmark.
generation.material_initial_state: Fresh 1 wt% multi-element alloy catalysts prepared from up to 19 metal precursors deposited on La-doped γ-Al2O3. These catalysts initially contain agglomerates of fine metallic particles and have not undergone accelerated thermal ageing.
generation.intervention: Apply a closed-loop, high-throughput discovery campaign using automated continuous-solvothermal synthesis (200–350 °C, 20–35 MPa, with high alkalinity from 25 M NaOH) and post-ageing activity screening, guided by machine learning and Bayesian optimisation to select catalyst compositions enriched in noble metals (e.g., Pd, Rh, Ga).
generation.conditions: The catalysts are aged at 900 °C for 5 h under cyclic lean/rich conditions with H2O, then oxidized and reduced at 500 °C, and finally tested over a temperature program (100–500 °C) in a near-stoichiometric exhaust feed containing NO, CO, C3H6, and i-C5H12.
generation.structural_mediator: Post-ageing electronic and atomic reconstruction that leads to the emergence of electronically coupled Cu–Pt cooperative adsorption sites while reducing the formation of Pt–Ni/Fe species. This is facilitated by the controlled low-temperature, high-alkalinity synthesis conditions which also preserve beneficial alloy/support interfacial states.
generation.mechanism: During aggressive thermal ageing, controlled redistribution of elements promotes a surface rearrangement where Cu and Pt form cooperative active sites. These sites are hypothesized to weaken overly strong CO binding, enhance redox buffering, and improve oxygen mobility, thereby boosting the oxidation of i-C5H12 and NO reduction. In contrast, less optimal catalysts may form Pt–Ni/Fe interactions that isolate Pt and suppress its catalytic activity.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to a Pd/Al2O3 benchmark, catalysts selected via inverse-model guidance are expected to show at least a 5 °C reduction in T50 or a minimum 2 percentage-point increase in conversion at 350 °C after ageing, reflecting enhanced low-temperature and total conversion performance.
generation.baseline: Performance is measured relative to a Pd/Al2O3 benchmark tested under identical post-ageing conditions and compared to randomly selected catalyst compositions and synthesis parameters.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies to 1 wt% supported multi-element catalysts (5- to 19-element systems) on La-doped γ-Al2O3 under the described accelerated ageing protocol and near-stoichiometric exhaust test conditions that include 500 ppm NO, 5000 ppm CO, 200 ppm C3H6, and 120 ppm i-C5H12. The use of i-C5H12 serves as a stringent redox probe rather than a full exhaust representation.
generation.uncertainty: While improvements are predicted based on the development of Cu–Pt cooperative sites, the precise quantitative contributions of these sites and their interplay with other elemental interactions (especially with Ni/Fe) remain uncertain until further mechanistic studies are conducted.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform automated light-off experiments to monitor species-resolved conversions (NO, CO, C3H6, i-C5H12) across 100–500 °C for both the newly synthesized catalysts and the Pd/Al2O3 benchmark after the same ageing treatment. Complement these tests with CO-adsorption FT-IR to detect changes in CO binding indicative of electronic coupling, and HAADF-STEM/EDS to assess particle morphology and elemental segregation.
measurements: T50 values for NO and hydrocarbon oxidation
Conversion percentages at 350 °C for target species
FT-IR spectra showing shifts/reduction in strong CO adsorption peaks
HAADF-STEM/EDS images confirming the presence of Cu–Pt cooperative sites and minimal Pt–Ni/Fe segregation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the new catalysts do not demonstrate at least a 5 °C lower T50 or a 2 percentage-point improvement in conversion at 350 °C relative to the Pd/Al2O3 benchmark, and if the expected Cu–Pt electronic cooperation is not confirmed by CO-adsorption FT-IR and HAADF-STEM/EDS analysis, then the hypothesis must be rejected.
